correctness.rationale: The multiplicative-order necessity argument and the LTE-based inductive converse were rederived, including the least-prime step, prefix divisibility, first-occurrence/cyclotomic equivalence, primitive two-prime characterization, infinitude argument, and counting bound. Exact bounded checks found zero mismatches for all odd n <= 10^6 and for 431,568 two-prime parameter triples.

originality.rationale: The complete Bailey--Smyth note, Kalmynin's full arXiv HTML, OEIS A006521/A136473/A136475, synonymous searches, later recurrence-divisibility literature, and the current SCOPE archive were checked. Existing sources provide the least-prime restriction, extension lemma, primitive definition, and cyclotomic factor tables, but no exact ordered-prime iff criterion or the stated primitive two-prime infinitude/counting theorem was located. Originality remains to the best of our knowledge, with explicit residual risk from older or poorly indexed literature.

value.rationale: The result gives a global structural characterization of all Novák numbers by their ordered prime-power prefixes, not merely a finite record. It yields prefix closure, a complete two-prime classification, an exact primitive criterion in that slice, and an unconditional infinite family with an explicit lower bound.
